instruction: Repair every open finding and supply the required evidence; findings close only when a fresh critic or the recomputed gates verify the repaired output.

open_findings.check: Net cash omits $34.1B marketable debt securities (and $42.8B marketable equity securities)
open_findings.detail: valuation.json uses net_cash = cash 22.443B + short_term_investments 0 - debt 33.366B = -10.923B. The 2026-07-26 balance sheet (snapshot/docs/periodic.txt line 263, 265; MD&A line 1828, 1852) reports marketable debt securities of $34,143M (US Treasury and agency debt; the company itself reports 'Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable debt securities' of $56,586M) and marketable equity securities of $42,783M. Debt is complete (short-term 1,000 + long-term 32,366 = 33,366; no commercial paper outstanding, line 1152). Omitting the near-cash debt securities turns about +$23.2B of net cash into -$10.9B. Recomputed with the code's own formula (both DCF and EV/Sales legs subtract net cash): debt securities only gives a blended value of $185.54 (target about $186, upside -11.5%); including both marketable lines gives $187.30 (target about $187, upside -10.7%, 0.7pp from the Neutral band). The rating survives, but the published target price is wrong. The candidate discloses the omission (valuation_inputs.json rationales.net_cash; note Model and valuation section), but disclosure does not fix the figure. No XBRL concept in the snapshot carries these lines (MarketableSecuritiesCurrent stops 2025-10-26; DebtSecuritiesCurrent, EquitySecuritiesFvNi, AvailableForSale* absent; values 34143000000/42783000000 not in facts.json), so the fix probably needs a controller- or code-level mechanism for filing-text balance-sheet items, not just a generator remap.
open_findings.required_evidence: valuation.json net_cash includes the $34.143B marketable debt securities (and either includes the $42.783B marketable equity securities with a stated haircut or gives a documented reason for leaving them out), with target price and upside recomputed; or a controller-recorded decision that accepts the understatement, with the note quantifying the target-price effect.
